A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OneDiffusion and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Their material can be reliably matched despite section moves and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation and prediction experiments in Tables 1–5, with additional qualitative results throughout the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds image-editing and subject-generation results in Tables 6–7, plus task-composition examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the per-view noise formulation, joint flow-matching objective, Next-DiT/VAE architecture, and conditional sampling procedure. The new task-composition examples use the existing framework without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Section 8.2 adds PIE-Bench instruction-based editing and DreamBench subject-driven generation evaluations. Figure 8 additionally tests reference-guided inpainting and simultaneous pose/semantic conditioning. These substantially extend the evaluated data and conditioning requirements; the original training and evaluation coverage remains.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds comparisons with Prompt-to-Prompt, Null-text Inversion, PnPInversion, Pix2pix-zero, MasaCtrl, InstructPix2Pix, MGIE, and EditAR. Table 7 adds Textual Inversion, DreamBooth, BLIP-Diffusion, and Re-Imagen comparisons. Comparator membership in Tables 1–5 is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new evaluations introduce background PSNR/LPIPS and whole/edited CLIP measures for editing, and DINO/CLIP-I/CLIP-T for subject generation, with fine-tuned and tuning-free comparator groups. Existing training and testing settings remain unchanged; further procedures for the new benchmarks are sparsely specified.

E4.justification: v2 adds two qualitative tests of zero-shot task composition in Figure 8. It removes the three depth-robustness examples in v1 Figure 7, while retaining the larger depth comparisons in appendix Figures 15–16. These are limited case-study changes.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added tables continue the existing practice of reporting point estimates; no seed or replication information is added.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results. New Table 6 reports OneDiffusion PSNR 27.49, LPIPS 56.67, whole CLIP 25.84, and edited CLIP 22.34; Table 7 reports DINO 0.692, CLIP-I 0.814, and CLIP-T 0.297. New composition outputs and removed depth examples also change the qualitative evidence.

T1.justification: The flow-matching definitions, interpolation schedule, objectives, and conditional vector-field argument in Equations 1–6 are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same claims of unified bidirectional generation and prediction, flexible conditioning, scalability, and competitive performance. The introduction removes the standalone dataset paragraph and depth summary without withdrawing the corresponding contributions retained elsewhere.

C2.justification: v2 interprets Figure 8 as generalization from single-condition training to combined conditioning. It removes v1 Section 5.7's explicit difficulty in extracting masks, boxes, and keypoints from generated images and its future-work qualification. The other principal interpretations and applicability boundaries remain.

D1.justification: Training stages, resolutions, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, hardware, dataset preparation, and appendix sampling details are retained. The code/checkpoint availability statement is unchanged. The added benchmarks provide no substantial new implementation or reproduction instructions.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a short inverse-problem discussion with three new references on sampling and guidance. Direct Inversion and DreamBooth are newly cited for the added benchmarks. The positioning against specialized and unified diffusion models otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the introduction and multiview discussion, makes localized language corrections, moves camera-pose evaluation into a quantitative appendix, removes the Other Tasks paragraph, and adds acknowledgements. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6–7 and composition Figure 8, removes v1 depth Figure 7, and relocates camera-pose Figure 8 as appendix Figure 7 alongside Table 5. Tables are repacked and Figure 1's caption corrects the understanding-box color. Most illustrations and the basic layout remain.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's qualitative editing examples and Unsplash-50 evaluation, Tables 6–7 broaden quantitative validation, while Figure 8 supplies evidence for combined conditioning. These additions modestly strengthen the versatility argument. Sparse documentation of the new evaluations and removal of the output-extraction caveat limit the gain.
